newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee eases on dlr demand from power firms.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee eases on dlr demand from power firms.

text.p: The Indian rupee dipped below 35.71 against the dollar -- for the first time in recent weeks -- as unexpected corporate demand for the U.S. currency emerged on Thursday, dealers said.
Dealers at Bombay banks said demand from Delhi banks exerted downward pressure on the rupee after weeks of upward pressure on the back of lack of corporate dollar demand.
"The demand came from two public sector companies in the power sector," said a dealer at a foreign bank.
"They were buying from two Delhi banks which in turn hit Bombay banks," he said.

The dollar demand from the two firms was estimated at around $50 million -- not a large amount -- but was about the same amount the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) usued to buy to prevent the rupee's rise against dollar in recent months, dealers said.
The rupee dipped to a low of 35.7125 on Thursday.
It opened the day at 35.700/705 against the dollar, the level reached after Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened to buy dollars at 35.700/705 on Wednesday, dealers said.
The unexpected demand from the capital on Thursday saved RBI from yet another day of intervention, dealers said.
The forward dollar market was lacklustre on Thursday, they said. The six-month annualised forward premium closed the day unchanged at 3.64 percent, they said.
